summary: Indonesia offers a visa on arrival — which can also be applied for online as an e-VoA — costing IDR 500,000 for a stay of up to 30 days, extendable once, to citizens of the countries on its list, and admits the nationals on its visa-free list (among them Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Brazil and Türkiye) for up to 30 days without a visa. Indonesian Customs says every passenger entering or leaving Indonesia must submit a digital customs declaration, which is free.

notes: Indonesian customs allows each passenger personal goods worth up to USD 500 duty-free; each adult may also bring at most 200 cigarettes, 25 cigars or 100 g of tobacco, and 1 liter of alcoholic drink. Excess excise goods are destroyed by officers.

The UK Foreign Office says those caught possessing, using, making or trafficking illegal drugs may face long prison sentences or the death penalty, and that cannabis and cannabis-based products, including CBD, are illegal. The Government of Canada says medicines containing morphine or codeine are controlled substances in Indonesia and cannot be brought in, even in small quantities, without prior permission from the Ministry of Health and the required documentation.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says credit cards are not widely accepted outside large urban centres and tourist areas, and to carry cash when visiting remote areas. The UK Foreign Office says credit card fraud is common and advises using only licensed currency exchanges, identified by a Bank of Indonesia logo and a QR code.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office warns of bag-snatching and pickpocketing, particularly in busy tourist areas, drink spiking in Bali, Lombok and the Gili Islands, and deaths and serious illness from alcoholic drinks containing methanol. It says volcanic eruptions occur frequently and advises following local authorities' advice, including on exclusion zones.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office warns of visa scams by fake visa agents and advises using the Indonesian immigration website to get or extend a visa; it says the All Indonesia arrival card is a free service and that travellers should avoid alternative websites or email links that request payment for it.

The UK Foreign Office says possessing, using, making or trafficking illegal drugs is a serious crime in Indonesia: the authorities have a zero-tolerance policy and those caught may face long prison sentences or the death penalty.
The UK Foreign Office says overstaying costs one million rupiah a day and can lead to prosecution, detention and deportation at your own cost, and advises extending a visa within the initial 30 days.

Visiting Bali? The Love Bali FAQ strongly encourages foreign tourists to pay the IDR 150,000 levy online before departure to Bali, at lovebali.baliprov.go.id; the levy voucher with a QR code is sent by email.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Indonesia?
faq.answer: The United States is on Indonesia's visa-on-arrival list: the visa on arrival costs IDR 500,000 for a stay of up to 30 days, extendable once for another 30 days, and can also be applied for online at evisa.imigrasi.go.id.

faq.question: Can I extend the Indonesian Visa on Arrival?
faq.answer: Yes, once, for another 30 days. e-VoA holders can extend online at evisa.imigrasi.go.id; holders of a non-electronic visa on arrival obtained at the airport, seaport or land border extend at the nearest immigration office to their domicile.

faq.question: What is the e-CD and who must complete it?
faq.answer: Indonesian Customs says every passenger entering or leaving Indonesia must submit a digital customs declaration. It is free and can be filled in from 3 days before arrival; keep the QR code to be scanned by officers at the arrival or departure terminal. Arrivals by air or sea complete it through the All Indonesia service (allindonesia.imigrasi.go.id); arrivals by land use ecd.beacukai.go.id.

faq.question: What is the Bali tourist levy?
faq.answer: Every international tourist who travels to Bali and does tourist activities pays a levy of IDR 150,000 per person, once while travelling in Bali, cashless: via the Love Bali system (lovebali.baliprov.go.id) before entering Bali, at the payment counters at Bali's airport and ports, or through hotels, travel agents and attractions registered with Love Bali. The Love Bali FAQ lists exemptions, among them holders of diplomatic, official and student visas and of KITAS or KITAP stay permit cards.

faq.question: Who can enter Indonesia without any visa?
faq.answer: The Directorate General of Immigration's visa-free list names Brunei Darussalam, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, Cambodia, Singapore, Myanmar, Laos, Timor-Leste, Suriname, Colombia, Hong Kong, Türkiye, Brazil, Peru, Kazakhstan, Macau and Belarus, as well as Singapore permanent residents passing through specific immigration checkpoints. Its A1 page gives a single entry with a stay of up to 30 days that cannot be extended or converted to another stay permit.

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: The rainy season usually runs from October to March. The wet season can be different in Eastern Indonesia, which usually runs from April to August.
Wildfires in Indonesia’s forests are most severe during the dry season, usually from April to September.
The rainy season extends from November to March, but heavy rains are common throughout the year.

countryFacts.payments.text: Credit cards are not widely accepted outside of large urban centres and tourist areas. Carry cash when visiting remote areas.
Only use licensed currency exchanges, identified by a Bank of Indonesia logo and a QR code.

countryFacts.safety.text: Be aware of the risk of street crime such as bag-snatching and pickpocketing, particularly in busy tourist areas.
There have been reports of drink spiking linked to sexual assault in Bali, Lombok and the Gili Islands.
There have been deaths and cases of serious illness caused by alcoholic drinks containing methanol in Indonesia.

Volcanic eruptions occur frequently across Indonesia. In the event of a volcanic eruption, follow the latest advice issued by the local authorities, including on areas to avoid, exclusion zones and actions to take if air quality is affected.
